summary: The starter prompt is clear about the high-level goal (Node.js LlamaIndex agent that fetches segment profiles from Azure DocumentDB, injects purchase history/preferences into the prompt, generates subject+body, and writes drafts back to a 'campaigns' collection). Environment/run constraints in the included skill_md (Node.js 24, DOCUMENTDB_URI, database name) fill important gaps. Several implementation details are left to the builder (driver version, LLM provider/model, exact document shape, seed script, indexes, README and test coverage) and will be chosen by reasonable defaults — so the build can start but will rely on assumptions.

rubric.found_in_prompt: "build a Node.js LlamaIndex agent ... that fetches customer segment profiles from DocumentDB ... generate personalised email subject lines and body copy. Write the generated drafts back to a campaigns collection in DocumentDB."
rubric.note: The business problem and demo objective are clearly stated in the starter prompt.

rubric.found_in_prompt: "Node.js LlamaIndex agent with a tool that fetches customer segment profiles ... Register a tool on the LlamaIndex agent"
rubric.note: Single-agent (one LlamaIndex agent) orchestration is explicit.

rubric.found_in_prompt: "Node.js LlamaIndex agent"; skill_md: "Node.js 24 with npm and npx is available."
rubric.note: Language is Node.js and the provided run-environment (skill_md) specifies Node.js 24.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Use the official mongodb npm driver v5.x (>=5.0, <6.0) and follow the documentdb-driver advice to implement a process-wide singleton MongoClient.
rubric.note: The prompt doesn't name a driver/version. The documentdb-driver skill provides singleton/reuse guidance but does not mandate an exact npm package version; the builder will pick a recent stable Node MongoDB driver compatible with MongoDB 7.0.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Use the live, reachable vector-capable Azure DocumentDB cluster described in skill_md (compute tier M30, MongoDB 7.0 wire protocol).
rubric.note: The included skill_md run-environment gives the cluster details and instructs to use the existing cluster and the database sample_retail_08.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Read the connection string from DOCUMENTDB_URI environment variable at runtime and do not commit secrets to the repo; LLM/API keys also in env vars.
rubric.note: skill_md explicitly instructs the connection string is in DOCUMENTDB_URI and must not be written into files; that determines where secrets live.

rubric.found_in_prompt: "fetches customer segment profiles"; "inject the segment's purchase history and preferences"; "campaigns collection"
rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: The builder will create/use collections: 'segments' (or 'customer_segments') documents containing fields {segmentId, name, purchase_history: [...], preferences: {...}} and a 'campaigns' collection with documents like {segmentId, segmentName, subject, body, rawOutput, createdAt}.
rubric.note: Prompt requires segments with purchase_history and preferences and a campaigns collection, but it doesn't define exact field names or shapes — the documentdb-data-modeling skill can guide modeling choices but doesn't enforce field names.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Builder will add a small idempotent seed script that inserts a few sample segment profile documents (each with purchase_history and preferences) into sample_retail_08.segments for local demonstration.
rubric.note: No seed data source or script is provided. The run-environment mentions using sample_retail_08, but does not guarantee sample documents exist.

rubric.found_in_prompt: "fetch customer segment profiles from DocumentDB" (implied query by segment)
rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: The builder will create a single-field index on segmentId and/or name for efficient lookup, and may add indexes recommended by documentdb-indexing. No vector index will be added unless embeddings/search are used.
rubric.note: The prompt asks to fetch profiles (queryable by segment); index shapes are not specified but documentdb-indexing gives guidance and would be used by the builder to create appropriate single-field or compound indexes.

rubric.found_in_prompt: "LlamaIndex agent" and "generate personalised email subject lines and body copy"
rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Builder will pick a cloud LLM provider and models by default (e.g., OpenAI: gpt-4o-mini for generation and text-embedding-3-small for embeddings) with credentials in OPENAI_API_KEY. LlamaIndex will be instantiated with those models.
rubric.note: The starter prompt requires LlamaIndex but does not name which LLM provider, model(s), or embedding model to use; this materially affects prompt engineering and embedding dimensions.

rubric.found_in_prompt: "build a Node.js LlamaIndex agent ..." and "Write the generated drafts back to a campaigns collection"
rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: The sample will expose a small CLI/ script entrypoint (e.g., scripts/run.js or bin/generate.js) which can be invoked like `node run.js --segmentId=<id>` and an npm script `npm run generate -- --segmentId=seg-1` as the sample invocation.
rubric.note: Prompt asks for the agent and a writeback, but does not specify CLI vs API vs web UI. The builder will likely provide a simple script to demonstrate the flow.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Do not provision a new cluster; use the live cluster described in the skill_md. If infrastructure-as-code is added, it will be optional and not used by default.
rubric.note: skill_md explicitly states a reachable Azure DocumentDB cluster exists and the sample should verify against that cluster rather than creating another.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Builder will include basic README instructions: set env vars, npm install, run seed script, then run the demo script (e.g., node run.js --segmentId=...), and show that campaigns collection contains a new document.
rubric.note: The prompt doesn't include exact run commands, expected output, or tests.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Builder will treat success as: agent can be invoked for a segment, LLM returns subject+body, code parses subject/body, and a document with segment id/name, subject, body, raw LLM output and timestamp is inserted into sample_retail_08.campaigns.
rubric.note: Starter prompt does not enumerate acceptance criteria; the reference list contains explicit checks that are not all in the prompt.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Builder will avoid provisioning extra cloud resources, keep secrets in env vars, and not attempt production HA or CMK setup (out of scope for the sample).
rubric.note: No explicit cost limits or non-goals were listed in the prompt; documentdb-security can provide security guidance but not explicit non-goals.

rubric.found_in_prompt: skill_md: "Never write its value into any file, log, README or test fixture; use a config file or `.env.example` with a placeholder, as the prompt asks."
rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Builder will include .env.example listing needed env vars (DOCUMENTDB_URI, OPENAI_API_KEY, etc.), follow a conventional Node layout (src/, scripts/, README.md), and use a singleton MongoClient as recommended by documentdb-driver.
rubric.note: The skill_md instructs to use .env.example and not commit secrets; other repo conventions (tests, README sections) aren't specified.

questions_for_author: Which LLM provider and exact model(s) should the sample use for generation and embeddings (e.g., OpenAI gpt-4o-mini + text-embedding-3-small), and what env var names do you want for credentials?
Which Node MongoDB driver version do you prefer the sample to pin in package.json (e.g., mongodb@5.x or mongodb@6.x)?

Do you want the sample to include an idempotent seed script that creates sample segments and creates any required indexes (yes/no)? If yes, should the sample also create a vector index and run embeddings, or keep the sample purely prompt-based?
requirements_at_risk: The fetch tool must let the agent query the collection by segment id or segment name — prompt does not explicitly require both id and name query modes; the code will likely pick one lookup key unless explicitly told.

Parse the LLM response into discrete fields (at minimum subject and body) in the Node.js code before persisting — the prompt asks generation but does not require explicit parsing/validation code; this may be omitted without an explicit instruction.

Write the generated drafts back with exact fields: segment id/name, subject, body, raw LLM output, and a creation timestamp — the prompt asks to write back to 'campaigns' but does not enumerate these exact required fields.

Provide a sample invocation (script or handler) that runs the agent for a specific segment id and demonstrates a new document appears in campaigns — the prompt asks for the app but does not explicitly require an example invocation or demo script.
.env.example lists every setting with placeholder values — skill_md suggests using a .env.example, but does not list every env var; the sample may omit some required env vars from .env.example.

The vector index dimensions match the embedding model's output — the prompt does not mention embeddings or vector indexes; if LlamaIndex/embeddings are used, builder must ensure index dims match the chosen embedding model, but nothing forces that.
Vector index parameters chosen for the sample's data size, and README explains how to change them — index tuning is not requested in the prompt and is likely to be omitted.
A seed script loads sample data and can be run twice without duplicating data — no seed/idempotent loader is required by the prompt, so this may be missing.
/search returns a clear error for an empty query and when the embedding call fails — the sample may not implement a /search route at all, and error handling requirements are not specified.
Search results include the similarity score — search functionality and similarity scoring are not requested in the prompt and will likely be missing.
Dependencies are pinned in requirements.txt (or package.json lock equivalents) — the prompt doesn't require pinned dependencies; the builder may or may not pin exact versions.
Unit tests run without a live cluster — no test harness or mocks are requested; tests may require a live cluster unless the builder explicitly uses mocks.

Infrastructure for the cluster is provided as code using the Azure DocumentDB resource type — the prompt and skill_md say a cluster already exists and should be used; providing IaC is not requested and will likely be missing.
README covers what the sample shows, prerequisites, setup, run, and clean-up — the prompt doesn't demand a full README, so a complete README may be omitted.

The sample uses the name 'Azure DocumentDB' throughout and no former/neighbouring product name — the prompt uses 'DocumentDB' and skill_md uses 'Azure DocumentDB', but the builder might accidentally use 'Cosmos DB' or another name in documentation/code unless instructed.
